steps_h2: Make a Box Mockup from One Package Photo in 3 Steps
steps_lead: One photo of the real package, one scene, then a square file you compare with the printer proof.

faq.q: Can I make a box mockup from a design photo?
faq.a: Upload a photo of the pouch, box or bottle you will ship. A design file by itself is not the source. The credit cost appears before the job runs.
Pouches, cartons, bottles, tins, jars and bags work when the package shape is visible in the source photo.

faq.q: Can a mockup verify printed colors?
faq.a: No. It shows presentation and composition. A printer proof or press sample remains the check for color, ink and small legal text.

faq.q: Will small label text stay clear?
faq.a: Dense ingredient panels and other fine print can blur or change. Use a photo of the real pack when the wording must be exact.

faq.q: Can I compare two packaging variants?
faq.a: Yes. Make both variants in the same scene and compare the front panel, outline and shelf setting side by side.

faq.q: Can I use the mockup as my listing photo?
faq.a: Use it for a setting or a launch concept. Keep a clear photo of the real package for measurements and for details buyers must verify.

faq.q: What does a packaging preview cost?
faq.a: Each product photo costs 24 credits. The total appears before the job runs, and a failed job returns those credits.

faq.q: Can I share the preview with a retailer?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no watermark and can support a retailer deck or a pitch before print production.

faq.q: Can I test a concept before I order prints?
faq.a: Yes. Use the mockup to compare a shelf, counter or cafe presentation before you commit to a print run.

faq.q: What source photo gives the cleanest mockup?
faq.a: Use a sharp photo with the full package visible and limited glare, so the outline and front panel stay easy to compare.
